title: The Day The Big Issue Launched With Five Vendors
conflicts: New York encounter 1990 (Big Issue history, Guardian 2020, DDN) vs 1991 (The Boar): used 1990. Roddick's 1992 ultimatum: Roddick says break even in three months or close, Bird says no more money and three months, Guardian says only he was about to pull the plug: used Roddick's version. Body Shop money (£500,000 over three years vs start-up capital) and London rough-sleeper counts (2,000-3,000 / 6,000+ / 10,000) disagree, so neither is used. Bird's circumstances in 1991 differ between interviews; story says only that he ran a printing business and did not want the job.
notes: Several detailed sources are The Big Issue's own publications (marked company-archive); independent support from The Guardian 2020 (via Yahoo syndication), Drink and Drugs News conference report and Cherwell. The five-vendor launch and Ray Gray rest on Bird's recollection. The June 1992 figures (150,000 copies, £25,000 a month loss) are from the magazine's own history and attributed.
